name: Titan Design System Registry
description: Machine-readable index of the design system's components, patterns and directions. An agent should read this before writing any UI and update it in the same change that adds a system primitive. Extracted from App Redesign/index_prodRedesign_interactions.html.

conventions.idiom: Plain CSS classes plus optional JS render modules — no build step, no framework, no TypeScript. A component is a stylesheet, and a function returning an HTML string where composition earns one. This is the same pattern titan-sidebar.js and form-render.js already use in production.
conventions.consume: <link> the two token files, then the component stylesheet, then <script> the module if there is one. Order matters: primitives, semantics, theme, components.
conventions.tokensOnly: A component stylesheet may not contain a raw hex or a raw px for anything themeable. If a value is missing, add a token to tokens/semantics.css rather than hardcoding it here.
conventions.workbench: /design-system/index.html renders every component in every state, every registered pattern, and a live direction switcher. Screenshot the relevant view after any change.

tokens.rule: Components read semantics only. Primitives are raw values; a theme remaps semantics onto them.

themes.name: Default
themes.description: The look extracted from the redesign — every semantic already holds these values.

themes.name: Soft
themes.description: Rounder controls, borderless cards, elevation doing all the separating.

patterns.name: Modal dialog
patterns.summary: A temporary, focused layer over the current page. The originating context remains visible but inactive beneath the design-system-controlled backdrop.
patterns.useWhen: Use for a short, bounded task that benefits from retaining the current page as context and can be completed or dismissed without navigating through multiple sections.
patterns.route: No route — opens over the current page
structure: A full-viewport backdrop dims and disables the originating page.
A focused panel contains a clear header, scrollable body when needed, and action footer.
The header names the task and provides an explicit close action.
The footer presents one primary action and only the secondary actions the task needs.
requirements: Use --modal-backdrop-bg for the scrim; never introduce a page-specific black overlay.
Expose role=dialog, aria-modal=true, and an accessible name.
Move focus into the dialog, contain keyboard focus while open, and return focus to the trigger on close.
Support Escape to close unless closing would discard a destructive operation without confirmation.
Lock background scrolling and keep the page beneath non-interactive.
Keep controls inside the dialog on registered design-system components.
avoid: Do not use for multi-section settings, deep navigation, or work that needs a durable URL.
Do not stack routine dialogs; move the task to a full-page pattern when it outgrows one layer.
Do not use a modal as a substitute for a cold-loadable destination.
examples: crm.html — New pipeline and Add team

patterns.name: Full-page settings
patterns.summary: A standalone settings destination that replaces Titan's global CRM sidebar and owns the full task workspace at a durable route. It is never a modal, drawer, or layer over the originating screen.
patterns.useWhen: Use for configuration with multiple sections, substantial editing, or its own navigation context—work that benefits from a durable URL and the full workspace width.
structure: A full-width task header provides Back, the settings scope, status, and page actions.
The global CRM sidebar is absent so the settings task owns the complete viewport.
A multi-section task may add one local settings rail below the task header; a single-section task uses the full width.
Sections flow in the page rather than being split across stacked modals.
requirements: The route must survive a cold load and preserve ?u=<persona>.
Fetch required data on the page; do not depend on a previous document having stashed it.
Do not mount or load titan-sidebar.js on the settings page; titan-sidebar.css may still provide the shared page shell.
If the task needs section navigation, keep it local to the settings page and below the full-width header.
Navigate in place. Do not depend on window.opener.
Keep page-specific CSS to workspace layout and compose controls from registered design-system components.
avoid: Do not use a modal or drawer for multi-section settings that need sustained attention.
Do not leave the originating board or global CRM sidebar visible inside a full-page settings task.
Do not create a route that only works after visiting the board first.
examples: form-settings.html — /crm/pipeline/:id/form; every form creation/editing entry point navigates here

components.name: Button

props.label: string — omit together with `icon` set for an icon-only button
props.loading: boolean — keeps the variant's fill and shows a spinner; not the same as disabled
props.href: string — renders an <a>; dropped when disabled or loading
props.onclick: string — inline handler name, matching this codebase's existing idiom
props.title: string — also becomes aria-label on an icon-only button
props.className: string — extra classes for layout only, never for restyling

components.usage: Every clickable action. `primary` for the one main action on a surface, `secondary` for the rest, `ghost` for toolbar and icon actions, `destructive` for deletes, `add` for the full-width dashed 'add a thing' affordance from the reference.
components.avoid: Do not hand-roll a button. The product currently has 82 button rules across 14 class names — that is the duplication this replaces.

variantNotes.destructive-quiet: Outlined, not filled. A "Delete record" inside a form the user is editing must not read as the page's primary action. Found on the record screen, which had already forked .ov-btn-danger because no filled variant fit.
variantNotes.soft: Filled neutral. Secondary is white with an edge, ghost has no fill at rest; a toolbar button must look like a button without competing with the primary action. The board header had this as three separate inline styles.
variantNotes.hover: An outlined variant fills on hover (--accent-subtle), recolours its edge and ink, and doubles that edge with an inset 1px ring — a hover that only swaps colours reads as a colour change, not as a response, and at 1px the edge is too fine for a hue shift to register. The ring rather than a wider border: border-width moves the label inside the box, and 1.5px snaps back to 1px at dpr 1.

components.name: Icon

props.name: string — a built-in Phosphor name ('caret-left') or a product alias ('back'). dsIcon.names() lists all 85.
props.size: number (px) | string (any CSS length) — defaults to var(--icon-size, 16px)
props.title: string — makes the icon meaningful: adds role=img + aria-label. Omit for decoration beside a label, which is the default and renders aria-hidden.

components.usage: Every icon. Colour comes from currentColor so an icon inherits its context. Source is Phosphor regular (MIT) — genuine upstream path data, not a redraw.
components.avoid: Do not paste a new inline <svg>. To change or add an icon, edit the ICONS map in icon.js, or call dsIcon.register(name, body, viewBox) to override one — including with your own custom drawing on its own grid.
components.extend: dsIcon.register('plus', '<path d="…"/>') replaces a built-in everywhere; a third argument sets a custom viewBox.

components.name: Input

props.element: input | textarea | select — the same class styles all three

components.usage: Any single-line or multi-line text entry, and selects. Wrap in .ds-field with .ds-field-label plus .ds-field-hint or .ds-field-error to get the labelled layout.

variantNotes.inline: .ds-input--inline — edit-in-place. A boxed field would draw a border around what reads as body text; the record screen edits 25 values this way. Shorter than a boxed field (--input-inline-height), transparent until hover, same focus ring.

components.name: Badge
components.usage: Status and category labels. The semantic four (accent/success/warning/danger) carry meaning; the five colour labels are for user-assigned categories and ship as fill/ink pairs so they cannot be mismatched.
components.avoid: Do not use a status variant for a category, or a category colour for a state.

variantNotes.pill: .ds-badge--pill — fully rounded. The default badge is a soft rectangle; several surfaces had independently typed 999px (ov-contact-person-pill, kanban-won-pill).

components.name: Card
components.usage: Any grouped region. Elevation is what separates regions in this system — reach for a card before reaching for a border. .ds-card-title and .ds-card-sub give the heading pair.

variantNotes.section: .ds-card--section — a page content panel rather than a tile: --card-section-radius (12px) and --card-section-pad (24px). The record screen stacks seven. Forking a second card class for this is what produced .ov-card.

components.name: Stage chevron
components.variants: 'sm' (compact editor chips) · 'first' / 'last' flatten the ends of the flow
components.usage: The arrow-shaped stage header on the board and the stage chips in the pipeline editor.
components.avoid: Don't set its fill from a token — the colour is derived from the pipeline's own colour at runtime (shadeFor/darken), so it stays an inline style. Shape only.
components.note: Found by auditing /crm/pipeline/:id. The clip-path polygon appeared four times with three tapers, and .np-chev in crm.html and pipeline-settings.html were byte-identical. Uses --first/--last modifiers, not :first-child: on the board each header is the first child of its own column, so :first-child matched all six stages.

components.name: Segmented control
components.variants: none — state is aria-pressed on the item
components.usage: Picking a mode: the board's kanban/list toggle.
components.avoid: Not Tabs. Tabs switch a page's content region and sit on a baseline; a segmented control picks a mode and sits in a track. Use aria-pressed so the state is announced.

components.name: Menu
components.render: declarative — data-ds-menu="<panel id>" on the trigger; dsMenu.open/close/toggle(id) for programmatic control

props.placement: 'below' | 'below-end' | 'fixed' — ds-menu--below aligns to the trigger's left edge, --below-end to its right, --fixed takes viewport coordinates set by the caller
props.item: .ds-menu__item — a <button> or <a>; add an icon element and it lands in the aligned icon column
props.meta: .ds-menu__meta — right-aligned secondary text on an item: a count, a shortcut, a state
props.separator: .ds-menu__sep — a rule, for the one boundary that must not be missed (a destructive action under harmless ones). NOT for group boundaries: a label after items already takes --menu-group-gap of space above it.
props.label: .ds-menu__label — an uppercase heading above a group. Takes --menu-label-gap of air below it before its items, and --menu-group-gap above it when it follows another group.
props.caret: .ds-menu-caret — the chevron on whatever opens the menu; rotates 180° while it is open. Also used by Split button.
props.anchor: .ds-menu-anchor — a bare positioning context for a --below menu. Use .ds-split only when there really are two buttons.

components.usage: An anchored panel of actions: a three-dot menu, an account switcher, the panel behind a Split button's caret.
components.avoid: Positioning is not this component's job — anchor it with a relatively-positioned wrapper (--below/--below-end) or with coordinates (--fixed). Baking position in is what made all three existing copies re-declare everything. Do not use it for navigation between pages; that is the sidebar.

variantNotes.fixed: An absolutely-positioned panel is clipped by any overflow ancestor, which is why a three-dot inside a scrolling list needs viewport coordinates instead.
variantNotes.behaviour: dsMenu binds by delegation on document, so markup rendered after load works with no re-binding, and it enforces one open menu at a time, outside-click and Escape close, and arrow-key movement. The three hand-rolled copies each implemented a different subset.
variantNotes.groups: Groups are separated by space, not by rules: .ds-menu__label picks up --menu-group-gap when it follows items or a separator, and stays tight when it leads the panel. A line between every group turns a list of choices into a stack of boxes and spends the strongest separator available on the weakest boundary.

components.name: Split button
components.module: components/menu.js — the caret's panel is a Menu

props.variant: inherited — put the same .ds-btn--* on both halves; primary, secondary and soft all work
props.main: .ds-split > .ds-btn:first-child — the default action, unchanged from a plain button
props.toggle: the second .ds-btn — carries data-ds-menu, aria-haspopup="menu" and aria-expanded
props.caret: .ds-menu-caret on the icon — defined by Menu, since the state it shows is the menu's

components.usage: A primary action with rarer, related actions behind a caret — "Add opportunity" plus "Import records from sources". One control, one visual weight in the toolbar.
components.avoid: Only when the second action belongs to the first. Unrelated actions are unrelated buttons; a caret is not a place to park a toolbar. Both halves must carry the same variant, or the seam shows.

variantNotes.not a new button: Both halves are real .ds-btn, so height, weight, radius and press behaviour come from --btn-*. This file owns only the seam — squared inner corners, the divider, and pressing as one control.
variantNotes.divider: Mixed from currentColor rather than declared per variant, so a filled primary gets a translucent white line and an outlined secondary a grey one, with no variant per case.
variantNotes.brand colour: A pipeline's own colour reaches the split by setting --accent-primary on the wrapper, not a background on one half — fill, border and hover all follow from the one property. See crm.html's board header.

components.name: Pipeline tag
components.render: dsPipelineTag({ name, color, size, className }) -> html string

props.name: string — the pipeline's name
props.color: string — the pipeline's own colour, applied as the --pipe custom property
props.variant: 'tab' (class .ds-pipeline-tag--tab) — the folder-tab shape, for a tag that sits on a container's top edge
props.className: string — extra classes for layout only, never for restyling

parts.mark: .ds-pipeline-tag__mark — the pipeline glyph, in --pipe at full strength
parts.name: .ds-pipeline-tag__name — truncates rather than widening its container

components.usage: Naming a pipeline where a record's field list, a panel or a confirmation needs to say which pipeline it belongs to. The colour is data, handed in as --pipe, so the fill and border are mixed from the pipeline's own colour rather than picked from a palette.
components.avoid: Not for navigation — the sidebar's pipeline rows are titan-sidebar.css and stay there. Not a Badge variant: badge colours are fixed palette entries and a pipeline's colour is arbitrary. The tab variant does not position itself; a tab floating a hairline above its container is the tell that the caller skipped the overlap.

variantNotes.sm: .ds-pipeline-tag--sm — inline in a dense header or a line of text. Shape only; same colours and structure.
variantNotes.tab: ds-pipeline-tag--tab — top corners rounded, bottom corners square, bottom border dropped, so the tag and the container below it read as one shape rather than a label parked on a box. Placement is the caller's, as with Menu: put it on the container's top edge (translateY(-100%), flush to the side it belongs to) and square that corner of the container. /crm/forms builds its rows this way.

inventory.note: The fundamental building blocks of this UI, derived by surveying every CSS rule in the CRM (756 distinct class-rule roots) and clustering by role. `status` is the honest state: built = a component exists and is consumable; planned = the block is real and recurring but each page still hand-rolls it; excluded = deliberately not a component. `evidence` is the duplication a block would absorb — it is also the priority signal.
inventory.surveyed: crm.html, dashboard.html, opportunity-view.html, the directory and settings pages, titan-sidebar, crm-directory, form-builder, form-render, integrations, index.html

blocks.name: Button
blocks.evidence: 66 CRM call sites, 18 of them on the component
blocks.note: ao-, np-, ps-, os-, opp-, dir-, fl-, dash-, footer- … all the same button.

blocks.name: Icon
blocks.evidence: 102 CRM call sites, 58 of them on the component
blocks.note: 27 inline SVGs remain and most are deliberate: kanban status fills and the chart ring are data geometry; LinkedIn/Instagram/AI sparkles are brand marks; the pipeline chevron interpolates the pipeline colour; the circle-check is a checkbox affordance. form.html keeps one inline tick because it is the public page and must not load a 57KB module. Genuinely convertible leftovers: globe, download, arrow up-right/down-left — no equivalent in the set yet.

blocks.name: Input / field
blocks.evidence: 119 CRM call sites, 22 of them on the component
blocks.note: Covers input, textarea and select; ds-field adds label/hint/error.

blocks.name: Badge / chip / pill
blocks.evidence: 40 CRM call sites, 3 of them on the component
blocks.note: Status four + five category fill/ink pairs.

blocks.name: Card / panel
blocks.evidence: 53 CRM call sites, 7 of them on the component
blocks.note: Elevation separates regions; border is a hairline, not the mechanism.

blocks.name: List row
blocks.whereToday: email-tile, crm-activity-row, opp-activity-row, tile, thread-*, kanban-card …
blocks.note: Counted under email-tile, crm-activity-row, opp-activity-row and dir-row. email-tile and thread-* are MAILBOX classes that still have 35 CSS rules inside crm.html (thread-*: 25 rules, 0 markup uses) — leaked chrome like the composer was, not CRM list rows. Remove those and this block shrinks.

blocks.name: Modal / dialog
blocks.note: The Modal dialog pattern defines when and how to use the interaction. The reusable overlay + panel + head/body/foot component remains planned; modal scrims already share --modal-backdrop-bg. fb-overlay is legacy compatibility CSS and has no product call site.

blocks.name: Section header / toolbar
blocks.note: Title + optional meta + right-aligned actions. board-header's stacking bug came from every page rebuilding this.

blocks.name: Menu / dropdown
blocks.note: Anchored panel, item, separator, danger item, outside-click close.

blocks.name: Avatar
blocks.note: Initial + optional image + size + colour-from-name. Facepile is a stack of these.

blocks.name: Divider
blocks.note: Horizontal and vertical, one hairline token. Trivial, and reinvented 20 times.

blocks.name: Checkbox / toggle / radio
blocks.evidence: 21 CRM rules across 5 prefixes; 1 prefix mailbox-only, out of scope
blocks.whereToday: dash-toggle, fb-toggle, np-radio, tab-checkbox-wrap, crm-act-check, pl-*
blocks.note: dash-toggle (5 rules) is tokenised and reads --checkbox-size / --checkbox-accent; fb-toggle, np-radio, tab-checkbox-wrap and crm-act-check are still literals. Native <input> + accent-color throughout — no component exists.

blocks.name: Empty state
blocks.whereToday: dash-empty, dir-empty, kanban-empty, tf-empty, fl-empty, thread-empty-state
blocks.note: Icon + line + optional action. Currently a bare <div> with a grey string on every page.

blocks.name: Toast / inline note
blocks.note: Transient toast and persistent inline note are two different things wearing one name.

blocks.name: Tooltip
blocks.note: Missed by the original 27-block survey because it has no class of its own — it is an ::after on a [data-tip] attribute, so a class-rule census could not see it. Found while migrating the record screen.

blocks.name: Meter / progress
blocks.note: A ratio against a limit. Note the dashboard's KPI meters were deleted for being ratios against nothing.

blocks.name: Link
blocks.note: Inline link and 'add another' link are distinct; both keep getting redrawn.

blocks.name: Tabs
blocks.note: Underline tabs (dashboard type switch) and segmented control (board view toggle) are different blocks.

blocks.name: Table
blocks.note: Header row, body row, numeric cell, truncating cell, sticky header.

blocks.name: Nav item
blocks.note: Already centralised in the sidebar component but not registered here, so it reads as unowned.

blocks.name: Kanban card
blocks.note: CSS is fully tokenised and a direction can restyle the board, but there is still no component: renderCard() builds each card as an innerHTML string, so componentising it means a dsKanbanCard() module.

blocks.name: Kanban column
blocks.note: Stage-header colour is intentionally NOT a token: renderBoard() derives it from the pipeline colour via darken()/shadeFor(), which is data, not theme.

blocks.name: Side panel / drawer
blocks.note: Opens beside content and pushes it rather than covering it — a stated layout premise.

blocks.name: Stat tile
blocks.note: Label + value + context line. Deliberately not a chart.

blocks.name: Search bar
blocks.note: Input + icon + optional scope dropdown.

blocks.name: Split button
blocks.evidence: no class prefixes recorded by the survey; scale unmeasured
blocks.note: Primary action plus a chevron opening a menu.

blocks.name: Chart marks
blocks.evidence: donut ring, pie wedges, stacked bar, dot plot, histogram
blocks.note: Not icons and not components — data geometry. Owned by the dataviz rules, not this registry.

blocks.name: Brand marks
blocks.evidence: LinkedIn, Instagram, Drive, HTML badge, Titan logo
blocks.note: No Phosphor equivalent. Register via dsIcon.register() or keep as assets; never redraw inline.

inventory.scope: The CRM and its modules. index.html (the mailbox) is out of scope.
